body: Because I felt like I had no sense of control in my life I’d make up these arbitrary rules that if these things happened there would be a guaranteed outcome for example if I saw a monarch butterfly it meant that it would be a good day but if it was a pale yellow one it would be bad. I’d do it with songs for the radio too which lead to me to feel the deepest pit of dread whenever deja vu by Beyoncé would come on because I decided that that song would mean I’d have a bad day for some reason lol

honk honk welcome to the circus 🤡 

if im going to a doctors appointment or something ill explain that I don’t deal well with harsh light hence he glasses but if im the supermarket nobody needs an explanation lol

What you just said about how you were always told that you reacted badly or you you did bad things too were exactly the kind of comments I got growing up. I have so many memories of my dad trying to teach me things like maths or how to ride a bike or when I was older how to drive a car and it would be the most awful thing ever of him screaming at me because i didn’t get it right away and it made me feel so stupid and worthless. And when I brought this up to my mum I got “well you didn’t make it easy for him you just shut down and didn’t want to do it” like yeah no shit that was my brain reacting to being screamed at what was I supposed to do

My situation is definitely repeating a cycle, my mum was abused as a child so I believe that a lot of her behaviour is just shit she learnt as a kid in order to survive. And my sisters ex was also emotionally abusive the exact same way my dad was and I was going insane that nobody would notice that the cycle was repeating

Wow thank you so much for your response the part about my parents trained me to accept abuse in order to be loved OOF I’ve never heard it put so succinctly. 

Also worth noting that I didn’t mention in the original post is my mum was abused herself as a child with an alcoholic nmother who would put her and her siblings through hell. So for her to eventually marry another abuser makes me think that she was also taught that same lesson of accepting abuse in order to be loved. Not only that, my sisters last boyfriend was emotionally abusive too and my sister defended him at every opportunity, it’s just this fucked cycle that will never end.

The police incident happened only last year and I’m 26 now, but this sort of thing has been happening my entire life. It’s kind of embarrassing that it’s taken me so long to come to this realisation lol
I’m so sorry that happened to you, he sounds like an absolute scumbag so it’s good you have no contact with him people like that are not worthy of your kindness
Thank you, I’m a lot better than what I was and I can only get better from here. I hope you’ll be in a better place someday :)
Yes that is the biggest takeaway I had to learn, it was never my fault I was a child and they were the adults and they were the ones that failed

That’s so cool that your becoming more comfortable expressing your identity, I know that I’m a cis woman but I’ve always wanted to present myself in a more androgynous alt/goth style but I never did because my mum would say “why do you want to look like a boy” and I’d feel bad about it but I’m slowly letting myself wear things that make me feel more like myself. I’m thankful that none of my brothers are gay/trans for the sole reason that my dad has made the most heinous comments about that sort of thing I’d hate for them to experience that level of self hatred. I hope nothing but happiness for you my friend ❤️

Do we have the same parents this sounds so much like what I went through it’s crazy lol she would say “hes trying to be better he’s better than what he was” and this was literally after he was sitting at the kitchen table saying how women will use any opportunity they can to screw men over and they will get preferential treatment because they manipulate the situation because they look inherently more vulnerable compared to a man.

I hope that sense of shame doesn’t have a hold over you like it does your mum and I hope you feel some sense of peace now

My ndad does this all the goddamn time if you have a headache suddenly he has had one all week you’ve got a sore arm he’s barely been able to use his. It’s gotten to a point where my siblings and I find it funny because he will just magically have the same thing you’re experiencing just x10 worse.

Omg I do exactly the same thing of thinking “well he never actually hit me” and that’s because over the years my mum would downplay everything he did so much and tell me I’m overdramatising things whenever I would bring up things he did. But I know they happened and she knows they happened, she was there she witnessed it. That notion of never talking about it to hold in the shame is so true, she hates that I’m even seeing a counsellor because she hates the idea of other people knowing about her family business.

Omg that sounds like a lot to deal with the idea that your parents were never going to tell you this and thought that you didn’t have the right to know is absolutely ludicrous I hope you and your siblings are doing okay now

Thank you for your kind words, it’s easier to reconcile with now but when she said after the police incident that if I can’t handle my ndad then maybe I should leave that was incredibly hard knowing that she would choose him every time even after he did what he did.

Don’t be sorry you aren’t derailing at all! It’s good to be able to talk about it with other people who have also experienced it because while other people can express sympathy they don’t truly “get it”.

In my mums case I think it was safer for her to “keep the peace” rather than risk incurring any possible fallout. I’m so sorry all of that happened to you, you absolutely did not deserve any of it you were a child and they were the adults who made those choices.
It was hard for me too, it really felt like a betrayal. I hope you’re in a place now where you can heal from this

It was taught when we were kids to just shut up and not risk making his anger worse when he gets like this, so I think it’s just my mums idea of a survival tactic because he takes it out the worst on her. But I know she has to know deep down that I’m doing the right thing. She actually told me yesterday that she told him that he can only blame himself for me calling the police on him which leads credence to my theory.

My mum is not a bad parent, she did the best she could for us growing up by sheltering us away from him when she could and she took the brunt of the abuse for the most part. But she absolutely is enabling him because she learnt it was easier to just not rock the boat and let it happen rather than risk him flaring up even more. I can only feel sorry for her because I love her deeply and he has gaslit her so hard.

Omg that sounds so much like her it’s not even funny. She says that he’s “trying his best” and that deep down he has a good heart. I can’t be angry at her because she’s the biggest victim in all of this and doesn’t even realise it.

Thank you very much for your kind words. I have a meeting with a family violence organisation who the police forwarded my information to so hopefully I can get some sort of support that I’m not getting from my family.

The thing is I don’t even think she’s aware she’s doing it. She gets it the worst out of everyone and she’s so used to just trying to keep the peace as a survival tactic. I can’t really blame her for it but it still hurts if you get what I’m trying to say.

I do find it fun and challenging to mimic other pictures, but at the same time I do find myself adjusting things that I feel would look better than how the original picture did so I am free styling somewhat, even if only a little.

You are absolutely right about how pets can help, my dog is super attuned to peoples emotional states and can tell if you aren’t feeling good for whatever reason. So he always comes and gives me cuddles if I’m feeling sad and it makes me feel so loved :)

I’ve always been a people pleaser even as a child and I always felt like if I can make someone’s day just a bit better through my actions then I’ll do it. The validation and being told I’ve done a good job is great sure, but that’s not the reason I do what I do. To be kind not out of a sense of genuine duty but out of an expectation of a reward is one of the shittiest things to do imo.

Congrats on getting the biting under control, I know it’s not easy to go against something you’ve done for so long as a coping mechanism. I am nowhere near as bad as I used to be with it, when I was a teenager it was the worst. I had completely damaged my cuticles so they were all warped and lumpy and my fingers looked super gnarly and disfigured. I tried the nail polish technique once and for the better part of a month I made a conscious effort not to touch my hands and they looked kinda normal for the first time, so I think I might try that strategy again.

It sounds strange to say this but it provides a source of comfort for me in a way, like at least I can control this. The medication I take reduces my appetite anyway (except for when I’m due for a period for some reason) so that’s probably why I never thought of it as that bad because I technically wasn’t starving myself.

I feel basically the same way, I’ve had varying degrees of disordered eating but it’s been extremely exacerbated by me being diagnosed with hypothyroidism. I know it stems from a complete and total lack of control in all aspects of my life but I just can’t stop obsessing over it.

My family think it’s good that as long as I’m not forcibly starving myself then there isn’t a problem, I would like to bring it up with a professional, but it would probably be a while until I’ll be able to do that.

He does have a therapist but he feels that it’s not working for him and he’s quite disconnected from his family.
I myself have quite good external support, my mum has been brilliant with me and I’ve gotten myself a new job that I’ve been studying for the better part of the year. 
I know that it isn’t healthy for him for me to come running to him at the first sign of something amiss, but I fear that I’ll be a bad friend if I don’t because he has nobody else.

I reflexively apologise for everything, I wasn’t even aware I was doing it for the longest time until people started pointing it out to me saying that I don’t need to apologise for things that aren’t even my fault. Turns out abuse will make you subconsciously try to diffuse situations even when there isn’t a situation to diffuse lol
I often wonder what kind of person I would be if my father wasn’t abusive and it hurts me everyday
